hamzat al-waṣl imperatives sometimes carry the initial vowel (اِجْلِسْ, اُكْتُبْ, اُدْخُلْ) and sometimes not (اجْلِسِي, انْظُرْ); harmless, the engine still transliterates them correctly, but one convention would be cleaner.

summary: Checked all 16 scenarios (airport-checkin to school): every intro, culture note, dialogue line with its transliteration, English and segs, both mistakes pairs, all quiz items and answer keys, and every photo-scene spot and caption. The Arabic itself is in very good shape: case endings after إِنَّ / لٰكِنَّ / كَانَ / لَيْسَ, subjunctive after أَنْ and لَنْ, jussive after لَا / لَمْ, duals (تَذْكِرَتَيْنِ, وَالِدَا, الْوَالِدَيْنِ), diptotes (دَنَانِيرَ, صَنَادِيقَ, لُطَفَاءَ, أَسْوَدَ) and the number system (3–10 plural with gender polarity, 11–99 singular accusative, hundreds singular) are correct and consistently taught; all 64 quiz answer keys are right. 12 errors: 2 major (machines mistakes[0] marks the correct transitive اِضْغَطِ الزِّرّ as wrong and teaches a false rule; the phone-shop scene glosses the SIM-card label as 'the slide'), 7 minor tap-gloss problems where the dictionary sense shown does not match the object or sentence (أَفْضَلُ, حَضْرَةَ, سَيِّدَات, الرَّصِيف, الْعَرَبَة, الْعَمُود, السَّاعَة), and 3 engine items (the known quirks once each, plus a new one: وَبِالنِّسْبَةِ → 'Wabiālnnisbati', وَلِلرَّجُلِ → 'walilrrajuli'). The pattern is that scene-spot tap glosses come from a generic dictionary rather than the scene context. 11 notes cover inconsistencies (صَبَاحَ/صَبَاحُ, hamzat al-waṣl marking), photo/scenario location mismatches and clumsy English.
